label: recheck-b
tail:
Re-check complete. `research/frontier-15-alpha-b-recheck.md` is written; all three pairs are **ready for splice**.

## What the re-check found

**14 of 18 finding ids confirmed true of disk.** The substantive ones I traced all the way in: batch 4's two well-definedness lemmas are not just present but wired into the exact contract derivations whose route I said could not close (λ good-sets 1.1/1.2, the monotone-class complement and good-set passes); the unused Cantor/`lem-of-q-dense` edges are gone *and* the contract was rebuilt around the singleton injection, with all seven retained edges carrying a named use. Batch 5's three B witnesses and batch 6's rectangle corollary are real items with anchored contracts.

**Two dispositions were not true of disk, both in batch 5, both in the F5-x block the fix pass never mentions:**

- **F5-6 — not applied.** `cor-geometric-unit-circle-has-fundamental-group-z`'s `strategy` still ended *"must receive that id as an alias when the owner-approved un-deferral is applied"* — the instruction I declined. `items/rem-pi1-circle-is-z.md` still exists as a draft, so acting on it at step 5 would be an id collision and an owner-only id transfer.
- **F5-2 — half applied.** The `deps` are clean, but the condition that the agreement remark *name the two published pages in prose* had no carrier: the item had no `strategy` at all.

**Two new findings at re-check:**

- **B6-1's fix landed incomplete.** The newly minted `cor-goursat-rectangle-theorem` declared nothing supplying the filled-triangle notion its proof subdivides or the rectangle boundary it integrates over — contract step 1.1 had inputs `["given","construct","algebra"]` while concluding about filled triangles. A new item is exactly where this slips past, because no earlier review saw it.
- **A one-page extract was standing in batch 6's ledger as a treatment** (`math.ucr.edu/~res/math205A/nested.pdf`). Live URL, but not a citable document.

I repaired all four on disk rather than routing them — each was a false or unsupported instruction, not missing breadth. I also closed B4-4's pushback: Beta-4 rightly refused to write a book URL it couldn't fetch-verify, but that left a `proved_here: false` record backed by one unproved course-note comment, so I fetched and read Marker's *Descriptive Set Theory* §2 and added Corollary 2.38 (the strictness statement, with proof) to the ledger. The extract source became Schultz's full Math 205A notes §III.2 p. 50, which states the Nested Intersection Property.

## Gates

Everything green after my edits: `coverage-checklist`, `content-policy`, `splice-plan --dry-run`, `prosecheck`, `validate-plan`. Two checks worth naming — **129 of 129** contract quotes against published items are literal substrings, and item-count deltas (+2, +3, +1) match my approvals exactly, so nothing unapproved was added or dropped.

**`source-fetch-check --stamp`: 17/17 sources now fetch-verified.** All three Betas flagged this as their one open item, blocked by `ENOTFOUND` in their sandboxes; my runner has network. That run is also what surfaced the extract source.

One thing I'd flag as my own defect: my two step-3 artifacts numbered the findings differently (`B4-1` means different things in the review and the verdicts JSON), and the Betas read different ones. Nothing was lost — the report opens with the reconciliation table and both schemes are dispositioned — but that is precisely how a dropped finding hides.
